supersedes_diagnostic_versions.v1: identity-key mismatch made outcome join coverage invalid
supersedes_diagnostic_versions.v2: candidate pool restricted to immediately previous round and missed most target participants
supersedes_diagnostic_versions.v4: deterministic every-third-round sample; V5 evaluates all high-confidence rounds
supersedes_diagnostic_versions.gamelevel_actuals_v1: unioning all linked game IDs allowed cross-date exact-signature collisions; v2 uses high-confidence round-date consensus
supersedes_diagnostic_versions.gamelevel_actuals_v2: training used same-round rows whose lag1_pdk/minutes fields included the target label; v3 constructs each training row from the latest strictly pre-target candidate observation

game_level_actual_reconstruction.scoring_rule: Use target_pdk_round_total from the official historical Dunkest player-week-round archive as the realized player score. The game-level linked PDK reconstruction remains a secondary audit only and is not used to assign the target outcome to a single NBA date.

candidate_policy: For target round r, each candidate's latest observed row strictly before r is carried forward. CR, role and team are lagged; when a player has no row in r-1, the last observed CR is carried forward. Realized score is joined after lineup selection from the official historical Dunkest player-week-round target_pdk_round_total. Missing rows remain unknown in strict metrics and are zeroed only in the separate sensitivity scenario. Players never observed in the archived season remain outside the candidate universe.

target_date_mapping.mapping_method: Official-valid Dunkest PDK and player/team identity are used only to link historical outcome rows to candidate NBA dates. A round date is accepted only if >=75% of unique player-date links agree and >=10 unique links exist. Matchup features use NBA schedule and opponent defensive stats strictly before that date.

coach_policy: Historical coach CR is missing; use fixed coach_cr=10 for every team, and reconstruct neutral-credit base score from final NBA results. Coach budget and price-difference multipliers are therefore proxies, not historical market truth.

optimizer.formation: 4G/4F/2C roster; 5 starters, sixth man, 4 bench; one captain; max 3 per NBA team including coach
optimizer.reason: Historical carry-over roster and exact transfer/coach prices are not archived; this evaluates fresh independent round lineups.

training_feature_policy: For every training target round, all player predictors come from the latest archived row strictly before that target round. Target-round PDK is joined only as the label after prior features are selected; players with no target-round row are assigned 0 only in this explicit zero-inclusive proxy. Target matchup and opponent-defense context are joined from the target schedule by lagged team. No same-round PDK, minutes, box-score stats, or target-market role/CR are used as predictors.
calibration_policy: Player forecasts are calibrated using role x history-cohort residual means from expanding-season out-of-sample predictions only. Residuals are shrunk toward the global OOS residual mean with prior strength 20. The calibration fold never uses the held-out test season; 2022/23 uses OOS 2021/22 residuals, 2023/24 uses OOS 2021/22 and 2022/23 residuals, and 2024/25 uses OOS 2021/22 through 2023/24 residuals. Both the model and previous-five baseline are calibrated before optimization.
calibration_residual_policy: The calibration labels use the zero-inclusive proxy target: missing player-week-round rows are assumed to score 0. The resulting calibration is appropriate only for this explicit reconstructed-candidate scenario; observed-only rows are retained separately.
fold_policy: Train player score model on leakage-safe rows from earlier valid seasons only; test seasons 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. No test-season labels are used to fit its model. All high-confidence mapped rounds with a prior historical candidate pool are evaluated; CBC uses a 1-second time limit and 5% relative gap.
proxy_zero_missing_policy: Only for the proxy scenario, missing valid player-game PDK rows for previously observed candidates assigned to a scheduled team are set to zero. This is an explicit no-appearance assumption, not observed Dunkest actuals; strict observed-only results remain separate.
limitations: This is a reconstructed candidate-universe experiment, not a complete historical Dunkest market backtest. The candidate universe contains players observed earlier in the archived season; late additions and players with no earlier archived row may be missing.
The historical round archives are outcomes, not timestamped complete pre-lock roster snapshots. Candidate CR/role/team are lagged proxies, not certified market state.
Game-level PDK reconstruction is a secondary audit. Strategy realized player scores come directly from the official Dunkest player-week-round outcome archive.
Historical coach prices and exact credit-difference multipliers are unavailable; coach CR is fixed at 10 and neutral-credit base scores are used.
No transfer malus is applied because historical carried rosters and coach prices are unavailable.
The 2025/26 season is not used in this lineup comparison; tested seasons are 2022/23 through 2024/25.

strategy_proxy_bootstrap.stratification: resample rounds within each test season; preserve observed season sample sizes in pooled estimate
limitations: This estimates uncertainty conditional on the reconstructed candidate pool, zero-inclusive training/evaluation proxy, and past-only group calibration.
It does not correct missing historical pre-lock prices/availability, unknown coach credits, or transfer malus.
It compares fresh independent round lineups, not a sequential roster with carried players and transfer constraints.

v6_v7_paired_strategy_bootstrap.method: Paired season-stratified bootstrap on identical season_id/round_index rows. V6 is the observed-row-trained player model; V7 uses zero-inclusive proxy training and past-only role/history residual calibration. All realized strategy scores in this comparison use the same zero-for-missing evaluation proxy.
limitations: Zero-inclusive labels assume a missing player-week-round row means 0 points; this is a proxy, not official observation.
Candidate pool, CR/role and availability are reconstructed rather than certified pre-lock state.
Coach price and transfer malus remain proxies.

postselection_lineup_score_calibration.method: For each strategy, fit actual_proxy = intercept + slope * expected_team_pdk on prior rounds only, across prior test seasons and prior rounds of the current season. Calibration starts after 20 prior evaluated rounds. Slope is constrained to [0,2]. This adjusts the forecast score after lineup selection; it does not change selected lineups.
limitations: Realized outcomes use the explicit zero-for-missing proxy from V7, not fully observed official scores.
Historical market/availability/coach credits and transfer malus remain incomplete.
Post-selection calibration adjusts score forecasts only and does not change lineup selection.

interpretation: The zero-inclusive, past-only calibrated V7 strategy materially outperforms the V6 raw strategy and previous-five baseline under the explicit zero-for-missing proxy. However, the strict observed-only overlap between V6 and V7 contains only 5 paired rounds, on which V7 model averages 7.03 fewer points than the V7 baseline. The proxy superiority is therefore not certified; do not promote this strategy to production without better historical roster/availability snapshots.
